title: Refactor input focus styles and accessibility tokens for form primitives
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Over the last two quarters multiple teams have implemented ad-hoc focus styles on text fields, selects and toggles which diverge from the design system tokens. This causes inconsistent keyboard/visible focus, high contrast failures, and developer confusion when overriding styles. Goal: Centralize focus and validation states into a small set of accessible tokens and update form primitives (TextField, Select, Toggle, Textarea, Combobox) to consume them. Deliver a migration path for existing components and docs/examples for engineering. Scope: - Define 4 focus tokens (focus-default, focus-inset, focus-error, focus-disabled) and 3 validation tokens (valid, error, neutral) with contrast targets. - Update CSS variables and component stories. - Implement a lightweight helper mixin for runtime theming. - Add keyboard-only focus visibility behavior and automated Percy visual test for forms. Out of scope: full theme redesign, changes to layout spacing or form labels (handled in separate ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens documented in the Design System tokens page with WCAG contrast values
All form primitives use the new focus and validation tokens in Storybook stories
Keyboard-only focus indicator appears for form controls and passes internal accessibility QA
Migration guide added for frontend engineers with code examples and known gotchas
A GitHub PR updating component library and 3 sample app usages merged with automated visual checks passing
decisions: Use visible focus ring by default for keyboard focus and use .focus-visible polyfill fallback for older browsers
Adopt a color-contrast-first approach: token values chosen to meet WCAG 2.1 AA on typical backgrounds
Expose tokens via CSS variables and the design system JS token map to support Private deployments with runtime theming
Prefer minimal DOM changes in components to keep migration low-risk; use mixins to avoid primitive rewrite
